finding: The existing exact-run binding accepted claims labeled externally verified but did not itself verify the JWT signature. A deterministic RS256/JWKS verifier now closes that implementation gap before claims enter the binding contract.

primary_sources.observed: GitHub documents RS256 JOSE headers and claims including repository_id, workflow_ref, workflow_sha, run_id, run_attempt, runner_environment, iat, nbf, exp, and jti.
GitHub publishes OIDC discovery metadata and a signing-key endpoint for independent verification.

verification.environment: local Node runtime using repository-identical file contents

uncertainty: No live GitHub Actions OIDC token was requested in this run.
JWKS discovery retrieval, caching, rotation, and network failure behavior remain workflow integration responsibilities.

Signature verification proves token authenticity under the selected key; it does not prove runner integrity, same-process execution, transcript truth, deployment behavior, or physical-device behavior.
falsification_route: Accept a token whose payload changed after signing.
Accept a token signed by a key absent from the trusted JWKS.
Accept a non-RS256 token, wrong issuer, wrong audience, or token outside its validity interval.
Produce externally_verified claims without a successful cryptographic signature check.
